_why_setup: round-4 fix (was a hardcoded, never-seeded 'C:/some repo'). `cwd_kind: "my repo"` resolves to a REAL sandboxed directory whose name contains a space -- the space is the whole point of the case: it exercises gitcmd.repo_dir's quoted `-C "<dir with a space>"` parsing, which a bare unquoted -S+ prefix regex could never match. `${CWD}` is this case's resolved cwd (parity.py's _placeholder_map), substituted into BOTH the command text's -C value and payload.cwd, so the command's quoted argument and the real seeded directory are byte-identical. `setup: {kind: git_repo}` uses the builder's `at_cwd: true` default, which seeds exactly that resolved cwd (not a separate repos/<name> location) -- so no `name` override is needed to line the two up.
round-3 item 1 fix. A real repo makes the local half of the guard's work (branch parsing, cwd resolution) genuine; the gh response itself is now answered deterministically by U-0's gh shim (round-4).
expect_stderr_contains: BLOCKED (PR state): branch 'feature/merged-out' has no OPEN pull request
_why: PE-16 (round-4), same root-cause class as PE-14: git_policy.pr_state.message contains a backtick-quoted `gh pr view <n> --json state`. pr-state-guard.ps1 prints it from inside an @"..."@ here-string, so PowerShell strips the backticks at parse time -- a master defect. The port's message is correct (backticks intact), so full-stderr equality fails.

A bare `git push` carries no branch token at all, so this is the ONLY fixture that exercises the `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` LOCAL-kind fallback in gitcmd.current_branch -- every other fixture parses the branch straight out of the command text. The setup step's `branch` override is REQUIRED here (not merely for realism, like the other pr_state fixtures): _setup_git_repo's default checkout for name:'feature' is 'feature/parity-fixture', which would make the real `git rev-parse` answer a different branch than 'feature/x' and break expect_stderr_contains.
